lines.text: I've been thinking about your advice: go, see somewhere new. I've started packing. Slowly.
I told my cousin no. I'm staying. You were right: my life's here. Thursdays at the bath and all.
One season at my cousin's shop, like you said. I've written to say I'll come for the summer.
I went and helped my cousin, like you said. The shop's back on its feet. Family first.
"It's not your burden." I wrote that to my cousin, more gently. They understood. Mostly.
I sent my cousin an apprentice and some savings instead of myself. They're doing well. Your idea.
I apologised first, like you told me. We laughed about the teapot after. Thank you.
I gave it a few days, as you said. The steam's mostly out. We nodded at each other at the market.
I turned up with buns, like you said. My friend took one, then two, then hugged me. It worked!
I said what really hurt. It wasn't the teapot at all, of course. Your advice was hard, and right.
I kept trying, like you said. Third visit, my friend made tea. We're mending.
I gave my friend space, as you advised. Yesterday they knocked on my door. Space worked.
A go-between, you suggested. My friend's aunt carried a message. We're talking again.
I spoke up at the workshop. Politely, like you said. My hands shook, but I did it.
I worked harder, as you said, and kept quiet. My master noticed. I got the morning shift!
I found a new workshop, like you suggested. Better hours, kinder master. Thank you.
You told me speaking up was right. I've stopped worrying. My master's warming again.
I brought my master tea one morning, your idea. Now we drink it together before the shift starts.
"It'll pass," you said. It did. Like a bruise, just as you said.
I signed up at the potter's! Never too old, you said. My hands are grey with clay every evening.
Start with a cup, you told me. I've made three. None of them stand up straight, but they're cups.
I owe you something from my wheel, I remember. It's coming. Don't expect much.
Bowl number four! I kept going, like you said. This one only leaks a little.
My leaky first bowl holds dried flowers on my windowsill now. You were right. It's lovely there.
I swallowed my pride and took a lesson. You were right. I'd been holding the clay all wrong.
I let my little one join the Academy, like you said. They come home glowing every day.
We're waiting a year, as you suggested. My child sulked a week, then started training in the yard.
We visited the Academy together, your idea. The instructors were so patient. I feel better.
Bruises heal, you told me. I've stopped fussing. Well, I fuss less.
I talked to the instructor, as you said. My child's doing well. The bruises are from enthusiasm.
I asked my child if they were happy, like you said. Grinning ear to ear. That was my answer.
I knitted my neighbour a scarf, like you suggested. It's crooked. They wear it every day anyway.
Sweet buns for my neighbour's birthday, your idea. Gone in an hour. Perfect gift.
I asked around, as you said. My neighbour wanted a new tea strainer. Who knew?
Flowers from the Yamanaka shop for my neighbour. You were right; they knew exactly what to pick.
I said no to the loan, kindly, like you told me. My friend took it better than I feared.
I lent the money again. You said trust them, and I did. We'll see.
Only lend what you can lose, you said. I lent a little. It felt right.
Doubt was fair, you told me. I've forgiven myself for it. And I'm still eating those chestnuts.
I told my friend I'd doubted them, like you suggested. They laughed. They'd doubted themselves too.
I've just been glad, as you said. Didn't say a word. We roasted the chestnuts together.
You said change it. I've started an apprenticeship with the carpenter. Five generations of fish, and now wood.
I'm keeping the family nets, as you advised. I went out at dawn and the river was beautiful. You were right.
Nets in the morning, lessons in the afternoon. Your plan. I'm tired, but happy.
I gave my family time, like you said. Last night my father asked about my new trade. Asked!
I showed my family a plan, as you suggested. Numbers and all. My mother read it twice. They're coming round.
I went ahead anyway, like you said. It's frightening. It's also the best month I've had in years.
I kept the speech short, your advice. Two minutes. Everyone said it was the best part.
I told the river story at my sister's wedding. She threw a rice ball at me. Then she hugged me.
Thank you for listening to me practise that speech. All six times. You're a saint.
I spoke from the heart, like you said. Forgot my notes entirely. My sister cried. Good crying.
I said yes to my cousin's wedding speech, because you said I'm good at it. Now I'm terrified again.
I slept on it, as you said, and woke up wanting to. So yes, another speech.
I let my cousin's best friend give the speech, your idea. They were wonderful. I just ate cake.
I paid up my bet. A week of chores, done. Never betting against an Akimichi again.
I went double or nothing against the Akimichi, like you said. Now I owe two weeks. Thanks a lot.
We laughed it off over a drink, your idea. My friend forgave the chores. Mostly.
Another lecture on chakra theory at the scroll shop today. I nodded along and thought of you, my fellow pretender.
You always ask the question nobody else will. I tried it in a meeting today. The whole room sighed in relief.
Founding dates, you said. The history lessons. I still can't remember a single one either.
I asked the tax office how taxes work, because of you. They didn't know either. I was right!
Why do people grow up? Your question. I still haven't an answer. I'm working on it.
You asked what I think of you. I'll say it again: good company. Still true.
You were saving a question for me, remember. Ready to ask it yet?
Snacks before bed, our shared secret. I bought extra rice crackers. For both of us.
I caught myself talking to myself in the market and thought of you. I answered back, too.
Still skipping stretches? Your legs looked stiff today. Just saying.
No guilty habits, you claimed. I'm still watching. I'll catch one yet.
You owned up when you broke something. I keep meaning to do the same about the bell rope.
Our broken-things secrets are safe, aren't they? I haven't told a soul about yours.
Never broken anything, you said. Silk hands. I dropped a whole tray of cups today. Envious.
I told the shrine keeper about the bell rope, like you said. They laughed! They'd always known.
I let the bell rope rest, as you suggested. Some secrets are better as stories.
I bought the shrine a new bell rope and confessed with it in my hands. Your idea. Perfect.
There's a new puppet show at the festival grounds. Sad ending, I hear. Bring a handkerchief, soft heart.
You've never cried at a story, you said. I've found one that might do it. A scroll about a lighthouse keeper.
The storyteller by the bridge told the one about the faithful dog today. I thought of you, and teared up.
You told me you're sometimes jealous of a classmate. Is it still pushing you, and not souring you?
Not jealous of anyone, you said. I'm a little jealous of that.
You told me you feel it, sometimes, around people with families. My table's still open. Always.
Easier now, the jealousy, you said. I'm so glad. You seem lighter.
Comes and goes, like weather, you said. If it storms today, I'm here.
Your envy pushes you now. I saw you at the training grounds. It shows.
Thunder tonight, they say. Blanket ready? Mine is.
You're wary of deep water. Good. The river's high after the rain; stay in the shallows.
There's a gaggle of geese loose by the rice fields. Consider yourself warned.
Nothing small scares you. Not even geese? I'm still not convinced.
You wish you were braver, you said. I've seen you be brave since. I'm telling you so.
You wanted to be stronger. Whatever you're doing, it's working. I can tell.
More patience, that's what you'd change. Ha. I waited for you five minutes today and thought of it.
You'd change nothing about yourself. Good. I wouldn't either.
Getting there, you said, closer to who you want to be. You are. I see it every time we talk.
"Not yet." I like how you said that. Yet is a hopeful word.
You've stopped wishing to be different. I think that's the bravest of the three answers.
I wore my aunt's awful scarf today and thought of you. Some lies are a kind of gift, we agreed.
A kind fib that left you feeling awful. I know that feeling. My scarf knows it too.
You never lie, I remember. So I'm not asking you about my scarf. Not today, anyway.
Funny. Last time we talked, you said the exact opposite.
Hm. That's not what you told me before. Changed your mind?
Wait, didn't you say something quite different a while ago?
You've turned right around since we last spoke about this. What happened?
I remember you answering the other way. People change, I suppose.
Now that's interesting. A month ago you'd have argued against that.
You're full of surprises. You said the reverse to me not long ago.
Either you've grown, or you've forgotten what you told me. Which is it?
That's a change of heart. I won't hold you to the old answer. Much.
Both answers can't be true. Or maybe they can, on different days.
You said the opposite before. Choose one, and stand by it.
Ha! Caught you! You said the complete opposite last time! Which one's the real you?
You answered differently before. I don't think that's inconsistency. I think you're still deciding.
That contradicts what you told me earlier. I noted it at the time. I note it again.
Oh, you feel differently now? That's all right. Hearts are allowed to change.
That's not what you said before. I respect someone who admits a change of mind. Do you admit it?
Ooh, you've switched sides! What changed? Tell me everything!
Hm. Different from last time. ...Fine.
What?! You said the opposite before! Make up your mind! No, wait, tell me why!
You told me otherwise before. A person can change their mind. Just change it honestly.
You last felt strong winning a spar, you said. Win any more since? I'd like to hear about it.
You feel strongest helping a friend. I've been trying that myself. It's true.
Getting up after a fall, that's when you felt strong. I fell off a ladder today and thought of it.
You haven't felt truly strong yet, you said. Let me know when you do. I want to be there.
You faced your fear and it shrank. I keep thinking about that. I'm going to try with mine.
Not yet, you said, about facing your fear. When you do, call me. I meant that promise.
A little, every day. That's how you face your fear. I've told nobody, but it moved me.
Forgiving yourself is the hard part, you said. So I'll say it for you: you're forgiven. For whatever it was.
Other people are harder to forgive than yourself, you said. I hope that list stays short.
You forgive yourself and others the same. Fair all round. I'm still learning that.
You'd never throw a match, even for a friend. So when I beat you at cards, I'll know I earned it.
You'd let a sad friend win, sometimes. A gift nobody sees. I won't tell them.
Only at cards, you'd lose on purpose. Fancy a game? I need cheering up. Ha.
Showing off, your biggest mistake. Ha. I showed off at the bathhouse today. Slipped right over.
Not listening, that was your big mistake. You're listening to me right now, so there's progress.
That time you were unkind still bothers you, you said. That tells me how kind you really are.
You kept your biggest mistake to yourself. That's all right. It's still yours to keep.
You told the people you look up to. Good. I'm going to tell mine, too, because of you.
Write it on a card, I said. Did you? Too embarrassed still?
They know, you said. Words are nice too, though. Think about it.
That festival night in your favourite season. I hope this year's is just as good.
Your best memory of the season is training in it. Of course it is. Ha.
A quiet afternoon, your best seasonal memory. I had one like it today. I thought of you.
You hadn't had that perfect day in your season yet. It's coming round again. Let's plan one.
The best gift you ever gave was something you made. Made anything lately? I'm curious.
A meal you cooked, the best gift you've given. Lucky whoever ate it.
An afternoon together, the gift you're proudest of. I'd take one of those any day.
You haven't given that great gift yet, you said. Any ideas? I'll help you look.
Up in your thinking spot, dreaming big, you said. Any new dreams since?
You think about your friends, alone in your spot. I hope you think of me sometimes.
You think about nothing at all, up there. I tried it. Couldn't manage it. You're gifted.
Always planning what comes next, in your thinking spot. What's next, then?
Free ramen for all, your first act as Lord Hokage. The Ichiraku family heard me tell it. They laughed.
Visit every family, you'd do first as Hokage. Start with mine. The kettle's on.
Training the Genin yourself, if you were Hokage. The Genin today could have used you.
Fix the roads, your first order as Hokage. My cart hit a pothole this morning. Hurry up and get elected.
That nature suits your temper, you said. I saw a flash of it today, I think. Ha.
The most useful nature. Practical you. I keep thinking that's the wisest reason.
You'd pick a nature because it's beautiful. I watched a Genin practise today and saw what you meant.
You don't know why that nature calls you. Maybe the ceremony will tell you. I'm curious.
You'd want your friends to remember you. They will. I'll make sure of it.
The whole village remembering you. I looked up at the Hokage Rock today and imagined it.
Your students, one day. A teacher at heart, I said. Still think so.
Just one person, you said, whose memory matters most. I never asked who. I still won't.
Tell the instructor if someone blames you twice. Your answer. Sensible.
You'd face a blamer yourself. Calmly, I said. I still say it.
You'd forgive a blamer a second time. Big heart. Remember what I said about doormats.
You'd take a friend to your favourite spot, you said. Still waiting on my invitation.
Your favourite place is yours alone. I won't ask where. Everyone needs one.
Only your closest friend gets to see your favourite spot. Someday, maybe me.
You'd join a clan gladly, if asked. I heard the Akimichi talking about you. Nice things.
You'd stay clanless. Your own name, your own path. I tell people that when they ask about you.
Which clan would depend, you said. Decided yet? My vote's for whoever cooks best.
Become strong, to protect the Leaf. You're well on your way. I see you training.
Know everyone, that's how you'd protect us. You already know half the street. Keep going.
Keep the peace, your way of protecting the village. Hardest job there is. You'd be good at it.
Stand watch, you said. When you're on the walls one night, I'll bring you tea.
A found purse goes to the police, you said. The lost-and-found had a whole drawer of them this week.
You'd hunt down a purse's owner yourself. If I ever lose mine, I'll hope you're the one who finds it.
I've been holding my purse a little tighter around you. Joking. Mostly joking.
Ramen for everyone from a found purse. I keep laughing about that answer.
You'd return a rude person's purse anyway. Their manners, your manners. I quote you on that.
"Give it back with a look." I did exactly that with a borrowed umbrella last week. Very satisfying.
Let someone else return it, you said. It gets home either way. I suppose that's true.
You'd call out a cheat right at the shogi table. Remind me never to play you badly.
A quiet word in private with a cheating friend. That's how I'd want to be told, too.
You'd say nothing about a friend cheating. Loyal. I still feel for the old fellow in the park, though.
Worth losing a friend's temper for the truth, you said. Stubborn. I like stubborn.
You'd say sorry if the truth hurt a friend. For the hurt, not the truth. I hope that's how you meant it.
Let a friend cool off, then dango. Your recipe for an argument. It worked on my brother.
Here, the last dango. You always give it away, you said, so this time it's yours.
Half a dango is still a dango. Your rule. I split one with my neighbour today because of it.
One dango left. I remember your answer. Ready? On three, we race.
I'm eating this last dango quickly. You taught me that. Shameless, but fast.
You'd keep a friend's secret, even a worrying one. That's why people tell you things, I expect.
Tell an adult, if a secret worried you. Hard and right. I've thought about that more than once.
Talk to the friend first. That's what you'd do with a worrying secret. It's what I'd want, too.
You've kept a hard secret before. I won't ask what. I just trust you a little more for it.
Nobody tells you secrets, you said. Here's one: I hate the taste of green tea. Don't tell.
You'd rather not say about secrets. That was answer enough. I still think about it.
You'd stop for a stranger even with a friend waiting. I'll wait for you any day, then.
A promise kept over a stranger in need. Hard rule. I always know where I stand with you.
Help fast, then run. Is that why you always turn up breathless?
You'd give back extra change. The grocer short-changed themselves today. I sent them your way. Ha.
Keep quiet about extra change, you said. I count mine twice now, whenever you're near.
Spend the extra change in the same shop. I keep telling people your clever answer.
You'd wait for a hurt rival to heal. A win that's fair. That's what you said, and I agree.
Fight a hurt rival anyway, because they'd want it. You know your rival better than I do.
Ask the rival, you said, if they're hurt. Let them decide. That's respect, and I said so.
If someone blames you, you tell the truth straight out. Good. Keep that.
You'd take the blame for someone else. Don't make a habit of it. I meant that.
Give them a chance to own up first. That's what you said. More generous than me.
The long road, always, you said. My cousin took the shortcut last week. Came back covered in burrs.
Through bear country to save an hour, you'd go. Did you ever meet a bear? Tell me no.
Scout the shortcut first, you said. I think about that every time I take the back lanes.
A risk you regret, and you learned from it. Then it was worth something. Still true.
No regrets, ever, you said. Lucky or careful. I've decided it's both.
"Regrets come later." I said that to myself before I tried the eel skewers. They were fine.
On a mission, you'd walk past a stuck cart. The client's time comes first. Sensible, I suppose.
You'd stop to help a stuck cart, mission or no. That's how the Leaf got its good name. I said that, and meant it.
A quick shove and away. Your answer about the farmer's cart. Practical, like I said.
Sunshine all day! Your kind of weather, I remember. The training grounds will be dry for once.
Soft rain this morning. You said that's your favourite. Smell that? Wet cedar.
Snow's coming, the old farmers say. Your favourite. Snowball fight on the Academy field?
Big storm last night. You'd have loved it, thunder fan. I was under the blanket.
The scroll shop got a new adventure tale. Sea serpents. I thought of you straight away.
Training scrolls only, you said. I've got a story scroll I'm lending you. No arguing.
You read people instead of books, I said. I think you're reading me right now. Stop it.
I copied out a little poem for you. You said you like them sometimes. Don't laugh at my brushwork.
You sing badly, you said. The festival needs loud bad singers. Practise.
Did you ever ask the flute-maker by the shrine about lessons? I heard someone practising there today.
There's a musician at the bridge tonight. You're a listener, you said. Come listen.
Festival drums, your instrument. They're tuning them already behind the shrine.
The bathhouse is quiet this hour. Hot bath, your cure, you said. Go on.
Cold river after training, your cure. I dipped a toe in today. Never again.
Hot then cold, the old shinobi way, you told me. I tried it. My heart nearly stopped. In a good way.
Here. A smooth stone from the river, for your collection. It's almost perfectly round.
Found a rusty old shuriken in my garden. For your collection, if you want it.
I've written down my grandmother's pickle recipe for your collection. Guard it with your life.
Still got that button I gave you? The start of your collection. Ha.
Miso ramen, your order, I remember. Ichiraku's miso is extra rich today, they say.
Pork, extra pork. I told the cook your order and they nodded like you were royalty.
Salt broth, the purist's order. I tried it because of you. You were right.
Whatever's special, your order. Today's special is something with crab. Brave enough?
One bowl, savoured properly. I tried eating slowly like you. Lasted half a bowl.
Three bowls, easily, you claimed. I'd like to see it. My treat, if you manage four.
You've never counted your bowls. I have. I'm not telling you the number.
Here's my lucky coin. Borrow it for your next mission. You believe in luck, after all.
You make your own luck, you said. I've been working harder since. Luckier, too.
Only bad luck exists, you said. My cart wheel came off today. You may be right.
Well-loved over rich, your choice. Well, you're well-loved here. I'll vouch.
You'd pick rich, you said. Buy me dinner when it happens. Ha.
Earn both riches and friends. Your plan. How's it going? I can help with the friends part.
Get even, you said, after a prank. I'm checking my sandals around you from now on.
You let pranks go. The bigger person. My nephew could learn from you.
Flowers in the prankster's sandals. Your idea. I did it to my cousin. They loved it.
A truce with dango, your way to end a prank war. Worked on my brother. Mostly.
You'd win a prank war, you said. Leave my shop out of it. I mean it.
A prank war that never ends. I'm in one with my neighbour now. Twenty years and counting.
You'd rather lead. Mind you listen as much as you talk, I said. I still mean it.
Following a good leader well. You said it's a skill. Your squad's lucky to have you.
Side by side, no front, no back. Your kind of squad. Mine too.
A cook, if you weren't a ninja. I'll taste anything you make. Within reason.
A carpenter, you'd be. The Kinoshita are taking on helpers this month, I hear.
A medic, your other life. The hospital's always short of hands. Even for an afternoon.
A merchant, you'd be, without the kunai. Want to haggle for my old teapot? Practice.
Did you ask around about learning that trade? I know someone who'd love a curious student.
No time for another trade, you said. One day. I'll hold you to "one day".
You already practise that trade, a little. When do I get to see your work?
Front line, that's your place. Mind yourself out there. I worry, you know.
Support and healing, the role that suits you. I can see it. You watch everyone.
The planner with the map. Your squad role. Plan me a route to the market that avoids the crowds?
Scout, out ahead, quick and quiet. Is that why I never hear you arrive?
Your squad works like clockwork, you said. Still ticking?
Still working your squad out, you said. Any better after the last mission?
Your squad argues a lot. The closest ones do, I said. Still arguing?
A ninja dog someday. The Inuzuka had a litter born last week. Just saying.
A messenger hawk, you'd want. I saw one land on the Residence roof. Beautiful bird.
A lazy old cat. There's one asleep on the bathhouse roof that nobody owns. Hint.
No room for a pet, you said. Did you get a fish yet?
You'd stay out of a fight between friends. Safe. I tried it last week. It was lonely, like I said.
Side with whoever's right, you'd do. I had to pick between two friends today. I thought of you.
The peacemaker, that's you between friends. I've got two neighbours who could use you.
Wait it out, if both friends are cross with you. They'll miss you first. Still true?
Apologise to both, even if blameless. You're generous. I'm not sure I could.
"You're both being silly." I said your line to two squabbling neighbours. They stopped. Then laughed.
You'd stop for a lost child, training or not. The market mothers would adore you.
Fetch the police for a lost child, then off to training. Sensible. The police are very good with them.
A lost child at training with you. I'm still laughing at the picture.
You'd own up about a lost kunai. I lost my neighbour's ladle and told them, because of you.
Replace a lost kunai quietly, you'd do. I'll never know if my things are originals, will I?
Tell them and replace it. Your full apology. I did just that over a broken umbrella.
Ichiraku, best food in the Leaf, you said. Half the village agrees with you.
The dango stand, best food in the village. I told the dango seller. Free skewer waiting for you.
Akimichi barbecue, you voted. The Akimichi heard. They looked very pleased.
"Whoever's feeding me." Then I'm the best cook in the Leaf today. Here.
The next Hokage on the Rock, you said. Fair. I wonder whose face it'll be.
An ordinary villager on the Hokage Rock. I keep telling people your idea. The baker wants it to be them.
Your own face, next on the Rock. I looked up at the empty stone today. There's room.
A good dog on the Hokage Rock. The Inuzuka loved that, when I told them. Loved it.
The rules keep young ninja safe, you said. My aunt agreed. She wants to meet you now.
Too strict, you said, the rules for young ninja. Every generation says it. Mine did.
Some rules fair, some not. I've been sorting them since you said that.
A later curfew, your one change. The noodle stands would build you a statue.
You wouldn't change a single rule. Patient. I'm still impressed.
Open the forest trails, you'd change. Mind the boars if they ever do.
You said the Leaf seemed so big at first. Does it still? It shrinks once you know every lane.
"Noisy and warm." Your first look at the Leaf. I was smelling the grill smoke today and thought, yes.
Lonely at first, you told me. I hope it's less so now. I've been trying to help with that.
Like home already, you said, from the very first day. The Leaf has good instincts.
You told me the Leaf is home now. I've been smiling about that for days.
Getting there, you said, about feeling at home. Getting closer? I hope so.
Not home yet, you said. The lantern's still lit. I haven't forgotten.
Your best day here was a festival, you said. The next one's coming. Let's make it better.
Your best day was a day with friends. So let's have another. What are you doing tomorrow?
That training breakthrough was your best day. Has anything clicked since? Tell me.
You once told me your best day here was that very day. I still think about it. Made my week.
That test you failed, the hardest day. Have you retaken it? I'd bet you passed.
You told me about the day you felt alone. I meant it. Come find me, any day.
The fight you lost, your hardest day. You've trained so much since. I can see it.
You didn't want to say what your hardest day was. That's fine. I'm still here if you do.
You remember your instructor most from the Academy. Good teachers are like that. They stay with you.
Making friends, that's what you remember of the Academy. Are they still close?
Your first Academy memory: a failed test. Ha! Mine too. We're in good company.
The Academy lunches, your fondest memory. I walked past the window today. Rice balls, still.
A friend for life from the Academy, you said. I'm sure of it. Treasure them.
Your rival, the one you're glad you met. Still pushing you? Still annoying?
Glad to know your whole class, you said. I told my neighbour that. They called you a gem.
Nobody from class yet, you said. Any change? Someone new caught your eye at training?
Your first ryo went on ramen. I respect it. My first went on a paper kite that blew away.
First ryo on kunai. Still have them? You always seem to have a full pouch.
You saved your first ryo. Do you still have it? I'd want to frame it.
Your first pay went on a gift for someone. I keep thinking about that. It's a good thing to know about a person.
Still cozy, your apartment? I've got a spare cushion if it needs one more.
You said your place is a bit too quiet. So I'm inviting you to supper. Noise included.
Is your apartment still messy? Don't worry. I tidied mine yesterday and it's already a disaster.
You decorated your apartment, you said. Found anything new for the walls? The market had paper lanterns.
You told me you get lonely some nights. I remembered tonight. So: want to walk to the river?
You like the quiet at night, I remember. I'll keep my visits to the daytime, then.
You visit friends when it's too quiet at home. I left my lantern on, just in case.
I asked about your quiet nights once and you'd rather not say. I haven't forgotten. Just checking in.
Laughing till it hurts, with friends. You said that's your best kind. Got time for some today?
I saw a Genin fall off a training post today and thought of your mishap story. Sorry. Still funny.
You couldn't remember your last big laugh. I've been saving a joke for you. Ready?
You laughed at my face that time, when I asked about your last laugh. I've decided to be flattered.
That hard test you passed. I told my sister about it. She was impressed. So am I, still.
You're proudest of helping someone. That's stayed with me. It's the right thing to be proud of.
Not giving up, that's your proudest thing. I needed that reminder today, actually.
Proudest of making a friend, you said. I hope I'm one of them.
Your teachers tell you they're proud. Good. They're not the only ones, you know.
Nobody had said they were proud of you, so I did. I'll say it again: proud of you.
Your friends tell you they're proud. Count me among them.
Friends matter most, your big lesson. I told my nephew that this week. Credited you.
Hard work pays off, you said. Slowly, then all at once. I'm still waiting on the "all at once".
Asking for help, your biggest lesson. So: can you help me carry these sacks? Good practice for both of us.
Never skip breakfast. Your most important lesson in the Leaf. I haven't skipped one since.
A teacher taught you that lesson. Did you ever thank them? It would mean the world.
A friend taught you, you said. The best teachers don't know they're teaching.
You learned it alone, the hard way. I hope next time you don't have to.
The village itself taught you. Strict but fair, I said. Still agree?
A shinobi who protects people. That's what you told me you'd be. I can already see it.
Still aiming to be the strongest? Then you'd better finish that bowl. Strength needs fuel.
The cleverest shinobi in the Leaf, you said. Solve this, then: why does my roof only leak on dry days?
A shinobi who sees the world. When you go, send me a postcard from somewhere with mountains.
You said someone you admire set you on your path. Have you told them yet? People like hearing that.
You want to prove yourself. To yourself first, I said. I still mean it.
"I just know," you said, about your dream. I envy that. I've never just known anything.
Hard to explain, your dream. That's all right. I think I understood anyway.
You'd stay in the Leaf your whole life, you said. Good. I'd miss you otherwise.
You want to see the world. I met a traveller from the coast today and thought of you.
Travel, then come home. Your plan. Mine too, if my knees allow.
A whole year away, gladly, you said. I'd keep your seat warm. Just come back.
Only if your squad came too. Home walks with you, then. I liked that answer.
You'd stay rather than go a year. The village is lucky to have someone who wants to stay.
Future Hokage! I'm being extra nice to you now, you'll notice. Remember me when you're famous.
Too much paperwork, you said about being Hokage. I saw the stacks carried up today. You were right.
"Maybe, one day." I still think about your face carved up on the Rock. It suits the stone.
Someone better should be Hokage, you said. Be careful. Modest people sometimes end up there anyway.
As soon as you can, you said about Chunin. Don't rush past the good parts on the way.
When you're ready, you said. The vest will keep. I like that you're not in a hurry.
Rank doesn't matter to you, I remember. Rare, in a ninja. Don't let anyone talk you out of it.
Leading a squad in ten years. Be the captain you'd want to follow, I said. Still true.
A ninja who runs a shop someday. I've been thinking what you'd sell. Kunai and pickles?
Out on the road in ten years, you told me. Write. I mean it.
Ten years from now, here with your friends. I'm counting myself in that.
Fire's your nature, if you got to choose. Mind my eyebrows when you learn it.
Water, you'd pick. Calm on top, strong underneath. I still think that suits you.
Wind for you, you said. Felt a breeze earlier and thought of you. Silly, I know.
Earth or lightning, you couldn't choose. Still torn? The nature ceremony will decide for you.
Your dream home is a big house full of people. When it's built, I want a room.
A quiet place by the river. I walked past a little house by the water today. For sale, too.
Any home will do, so long as it has a kitchen. I respect that more every day.
Still dreaming of a tent, always moving? It's going to rain all week. Think it over.
You want to be remembered for being kind. You will be. You already are, a little.
Strong, that's how you want to be remembered. Strong for others, I hope. I think you will be.
"They always kept their word." That's your stone, you said. I'll make sure it gets carved right. In a hundred years.
You want to be remembered for making people laugh. Well, you made me laugh this week. That's a start.
Your dream jutsu is a flashy one. When you learn it, warn the laundry lines first.
A healing jutsu, if you could pick any. The hospital's always looking for helpers, you know.
A sneaky jutsu, you said. Is that why I never hear you coming?
A jutsu that protects. Of all the jutsu in the scrolls, that's the one you'd pick. I keep remembering that.
Ramen, you said. Ichiraku's doing a double-pork bowl this week. Thought you'd want to know.
I walked past Ichiraku and thought of you. Your favourite, wasn't it?
Here. Three dango, sweet sauce. You said they were your favourite, so I bought an extra skewer.
The fishmonger had beautiful sweetfish this morning. Grilled fish is your favourite, isn't it?
"Whatever's free." I have a leftover rice ball. It's free. You're welcome.
That hot pot you'd make for all your friends. When's it happening? I'm bringing the tofu.
Did you ever cook that dish you invented? I'm brave enough to try it. Probably.
Takeout from Ichiraku for a party, you said. I've decided that's genius.
The cherry trees by the river are budding. Spring's your season, isn't it? Not long now.
Summer's your favourite, you told me. I hope the festival this year is worth the wait.
You love the autumn leaves, you said. I pressed a red maple leaf for you. Here.
Winter was your pick, I remember. Brave. I'm wearing three layers and still cold.
Training alone at dawn, you said. I've seen the dew still on the training posts and wondered if you'd been there.
You train best sparring with friends. If you need a partner, I'll be at the grounds after lunch.
You like learning from the scrolls. The library got new ones in last week. Taijutsu, I think.
"Until I drop," you said. Please don't. Eat something first, at least.
Patience is the hardest part, you told me. How's it coming along? No rush. Ha.
Losing is hard, you said. For what it's worth, the best people I know have lost plenty.
You said trusting others is the hardest. I hope you know you can trust me.
Still at war with early mornings? I've got strong tea. It helps.
A morning person! I knew I'd find you up and about at this hour.
You're a night owl, I remember. You look half asleep. Too early for you?
It's nearly noon. Nap time, for you, if I remember rightly.
Raining again. Off to train anyway, I suppose? Take a towel.
Rainy days are for reading, you said. I've got a scroll you might like. Adventures on the far coast.
Rain tonight. Puddle weather. Mind you keep one pair of sandals dry.
Hear that rain? Perfect sleeping weather, you'd say. I'm half tempted myself.
You think best on the Hokage Rock. Was that you up there at sunset? I couldn't tell from the market.
The river's your thinking spot. If you ever want company there, quiet company, ask.
You think things through at the training grounds. Something on your mind lately? You can tell me.
Your rooftop thinking spot is safe with me. I haven't told a soul.
Something handmade, you said. So I made you this. Don't laugh. It's meant to be a fox.
You said time is the best gift. So I've cleared my afternoon. What shall we do?
The best gift is a good meal, you told me. Sit down. I've made too much again.
A new scroll. That's the gift you'd want most. I'm keeping an eye out at the scroll shop.
You're a dog person, I remember. The Inuzuka puppies are out on the green today. Go and see.
There's a new cat sleeping on the bathhouse steps. Thought of you, cat person.
A heron landed by the second bridge this morning. You'd have loved it, bird lover.
Any animal at all, you said. There's a goat loose behind the grocer's. Your kind of afternoon.
The food stalls, you said, best part of the festival. I'm making a map of them this year.
Fireworks are your favourite. I know a good spot on the hill to watch them. Next festival?
Goldfish scoop, next festival. You and me. You said you love the games, so no backing out.
You go to festivals for the friends, you told me. Then you'll come with us next time, I hope.
Explore past the gate on a day off, you said. Find anything out there yet?
Found a new lane yet, wandering the village on your days off? I hear there's a tea house behind the potter's.
Your perfect day off: sleep till noon. You look like you could use one.
A free day with friends, you said, doesn't matter where. Your next one, come find me.
Sweet tooth! Here, a red bean bun. Still warm.
You're a salty sort, I remember. I brought rice crackers. The good ones, with seaweed.
Sweet soy dango, the best of both, you said. I've been eating nothing else since.
I showed my sister's painting to a friend and remembered you: the truth, gently. It went fine.
You said you'd tell a friend the truth, gently. I've been practising the gently part.
If I ever show you a painting, I'll know you'd love it no matter what. Comforting, really.
"Ask what they like about it." I tried that with the potter's lopsided bowl. They admitted it themselves.
Still thinking about painting lessons with a terrible painter? I'd pay to watch.
You said you were grateful for a hard truth once. So here's one: you work too hard. Rest a little.
That truth that still stings, the one you mentioned. Does it sting less these days? I hope so.
You'd rather not have known, you said. I think of that whenever I'm about to say something blunt.
Rules first, you told me. The gate guards would adore you. I mean that kindly.
Mission first, rules second. Did you ever have to explain that to a sensei? I'd love to hear it.
"Some rules are walls and some are fences." I've been sorting the village's rules into the two ever since.
You said you'd follow the order and leave a teammate. I hope that day never comes for you.
I keep thinking about what you said: you'd go back for a teammate, orders or not. I'd want you on my side.
A third way, you said, when the choice is the mission or a friend. Have you found one yet?
Winning fights, that's strength to you. How many did you win this week? I'm keeping count.
You told me strong means protecting people. I think of that every time the night patrol walks past.
Never giving up. That's what you said strength was. I had a bad day and remembered it. Thank you.
"Knowing yourself." I've been chewing on that answer of yours for days.
You work best alone, I know. I'll leave this here and go. Call if you need a second pair of hands.
You said you work best with a team. I've got a job that needs two. Interested?
"Depends on the team." Have you found the right one yet?
I know you'd rather handle things yourself. Just remember that offer of mine is still open.
You told me you'd tell a friend when something's wrong. I'm a friend. That's all I'm saying.
Still learning to ask for help? Here's practice: ask me for something. Anything.
You said being alone frightens you. So I thought I'd come and sit with you a while.
You're afraid of letting people down. For what it's worth, you've never let me down.
There was an enormous spider in the bathhouse this morning. I thought of you and shooed it out.
Afraid of nothing at all, you told me. Not even my cooking? Brave.
A promise is never to be broken, you said. So I'll only ask you for small ones.
You said you'd break a promise to spare someone pain. I keep turning that over. It's kind, and it's risky.
"Break it only if you explain why." I had to do just that with my brother. It worked.
You forgive right away, you told me. I hope people deserve it as quickly as you give it.
Sorry is a word, you said, and what comes after is the apology. I've been holding people to that.
Some things take a day to forgive, and some take years. Your answer. I think about the long ones.
You'd keep the old customs, you said. The shrine keeper would like you. Bow at the gate, like the elders do.
You'd let some old customs go. One went this spring: the noodle shop opened on a holiday. Happy?
I asked an elder why we tie paper at the shrine, like you suggested. It's a long story. Want it?
You'd speak up to the elders if they were wrong. Just remember to bow first.
You said you'd trust the elders. I hope they earn it.
A word in private, not in public. That's your way with elders. Mine too, now that I think of it.
How you win matters, you said. I told that to a Genin who was gloating at the training grounds.
A win is a win, you told me. So, how many wins this month?
Anything goes against a bandit, fair play with friends. Your rule. I've adopted it for card games.
You count your friends here as family. I set an extra cup at supper. Just in case.
I've been thinking about what you said, about friends being family. Count me in.
Your squad is your family, you said. How is the family? Eating properly?
The whole village as family. A lot of cousins. I'm glad I'm one of them.
Still finding your family, you said. Take your time. There's room at my table meanwhile.
Own up at once, you told me. I did, yesterday, over the broken teapot. It went better than I feared.
Fix it quietly. That's your way with mistakes. I tried it with a cracked bowl. Glue and silence.
Learn from it and move on, you said. I'm trying that with last week. Slowly.
One day of sulking, then back to work. I've taken up your method. Today was my day.
Little lies are harmless, you said. So tell me: is my new haircut nice?
No little lies for you, you said. Good. I need an honest opinion on my new sandals. Ugly, yes?
The silent compliment. I used your trick on my uncle's new hat. Nobody noticed.
You look up to your teachers. Did you ever tell them? You should.
You said you look up to your friends. I hope you know some of them look up to you.
The Hokage, you said, when I asked who you look up to. Aim high. I haven't forgotten.
Nobody to look up to yet, you said. Then you're making your own path. Good.
Your favourite spot is Ichiraku, isn't it? I'm headed that way. Join me?
I went up the Hokage Rock because you said it was your favourite place. The view! You were right.
Your favourite place is the training grounds. Even on festival days, I bet.
I sat by the second bridge this morning, your favourite spot. The fish really are fat.
You wouldn't change a thing about the Leaf. I was grumbling about the roads today and remembered that.
More festivals, your one change. I'd vote for you on that alone.
Fewer rules, you'd want. Don't say it too loudly near the council chambers.
More help for the lonely, you said. I've started visiting the old widow next door because of that.
The Leaf changes too fast, you said. A new shop went up on main street this week. I see what you mean.
Not fast enough, you said of the village. Patience. It moves at the pace of its oldest elder.
About right, the way the village changes. Steady, like a river. I liked how you put it.
You think the clans keep the village's traditions. The Akimichi would set an extra plate for you for that.
Clan or no clan, the same headband. Your words. I've heard them repeated in the market since.
Clans should share what they know, you said. The Yamanaka gave a free lesson on flowers today. A start.
It's Market Day soon. You love the bustle, I remember. Want to walk the stalls together?
Market Day's coming. Too noisy for you, I know. I'll pick something up for you if you like.
The grilled corn man's back for Market Day. You said that's all you go for.
The people. That's what's worth protecting, you said. Not the walls. I agree more every day.
You'd protect the children before anything. I saw the Academy kids at play and thought of that.
The old ways are worth protecting, you said. My grandmother would have liked you.
Your friends are what's worth protecting, you said. Start close. I hope I'm close.
By the market, that's where you'd live. Fresh bread every morning. I'm jealous already.
The quiet forest edge for you. I walked out that way yesterday. Birds instead of hawkers, like you said.
Somewhere in between the market and the forest. The residential lanes. Very you.
Open the gates wide, you said. A caravan came in from the south today. Spices everywhere.
Welcome travellers carefully, you told me. The gate guards agree with you, by the look on their faces.
Friends, not strangers. That's how you'd greet travellers. I bought tea from one today and we talked an hour.
You'd run a stall at the festival. Decided what you'll sell yet? I'll be your first customer.
You'd just enjoy the festival. Someone has to eat the food. I'll join you.
Helping at a friend's stall, that's your festival. I've got a stall. Hint, hint.
You like walking the village at night. Did you see the lanterns on the river last night?
The old shrine creaked all night in the wind. You'd have hated it. Spooky, you said.
Straight home at night, you said. Sensible. It's getting dark. Off you go.
You said yes to the sea! I've still got the map. The offer's open. Pack light.
Duties here, you said, when I asked about the sea. Someone has to keep the village standing. I'll send stories.
I've still got your shell on my list. The prettiest one on the beach. Promise.
The sea, that's what you most want to see. I dreamt of the coast last night. Thought of you.
Mountains, you'd see first. A merchant came through from the north today with snow still on the packs. Freezing, they said.
Other villages, their food and festivals. I tasted a southern spice today. You'd have loved it.
The road itself, you'd see. A true traveller. I still grin thinking about that answer.
You love sleeping under the stars. Clear night tonight. Just saying.
You've never slept out under the sky. Clear night tonight. We're fixing that, remember?
Bugs, your problem with sleeping outside. I bought you a net. Now no excuses.
A safe life, you'd choose. My feet still itch thinking about it. Ha. But I understand.
Life's too short for safe, we agreed. I signed up for the long caravan route this autumn!
Wild now, a porch chair later. Your plan. I've picked out my porch. Thirty years from now.
Danger's too much when others could get hurt, you said. I turned back on a cliff path last week because of that.
No line on danger, you said. I worry about you a little. Even I have a line.
Turn back when you're truly scared. Your rule. I listened to my fear on the river crossing. Glad I did.
Fill in the blank on the map, you'd go. I've found a map with three blanks. Pick one.
"Why is it blank?" Your first question. I asked an old mapmaker. The answer was: a very big bog.
I drew a dragon in the blank space of my map, like you said. Looks fierce. Bit wobbly.
The sea first, past the border. I talked to a fisher from the coast at the market. Told them you're coming someday.
A big city first, you'd go. Lanterns on every street. I'll draw you a map of the one I saw.
The mountains, your first trip out. Bring warm socks. Two pairs. Trust me.
Wherever the road goes, your plan. The best plan. I took a road today just to see. Found a lovely tea house.
Going somewhere unknown is brave, you said. Someone has to go first. I keep telling myself that.
Foolish without a plan, you said. So I've started planning my trips. A bit. It helps, annoyingly.
A bit of both, brave and foolish. Your honest answer. Like most of my best days.
Just past the gate, so far. Every road starts there, I said. Go a little further next time.
You've been out on a mission! The road gets into you. Has it got into you yet?
Nowhere yet, you said. Still jealous. The first time is coming for you.
Out past the village, you felt free. I've been thinking about that word ever since.
A little scared, out there. Everyone is the first time. You were paying attention. Good.
You missed home out there. That's how you know where home is. I said it, and I meant it.
You haven't been out yet. Still waiting for you, the road. Lucky.
How jutsu work, your big question. I asked a Chunin today. They talked for an hour. I understood a minute of it.
How the stars move. I borrowed a star chart from the scroll keepers. Want to look tonight?
How people think. I watched the market crowd today for an hour. Still no answer. Lovely puzzle.
I tried to find out how ramen broth is made, like you wanted. They chased me out of the kitchen. Ha!
You found out a little about your puzzle! You still owe me the diagrams.
Still wondering about your puzzle? Good. I'm still wondering about mine.
More complicated than you thought, you said. That means you're close. Any closer?
You never believe rumours. I heard a wild one today and thought: what would you say? So I didn't swallow it.
Some rumours are true, you said. The trick is which. I've been keeping a tally. It's about half.
Only the fun rumours, you believe. There's a fun one about a giant carp in the river. True, do you think?
How does Lord Hokage do it all? Your question. I saw the lamp in the office window at midnight. Still wondering.
Lord Hokage's favourite food, your question. I've heard three different answers at the market. I'm investigating.
You'd ask to see the Hokage's office. I walked past it today and looked up. Must be some view.
Who taught Lord Hokage? Your question. I've been reading about it. Every teacher had a teacher, you know.
Learned any new moves since you told me? Show me. Not near the pots.
You learned something about a friend, last time. Learned anything new about me lately?
You hadn't learned anything yet, that day. So: here's something. Herons sleep on one leg.
You learned a new word, last time. I've got one for you today: "crepuscular". Look it up.
A surprise about the village, last week. Found any new ones? There's always another.
You surprised yourself, you said. Good surprise or bad? You never said. I'm still curious.
A surprise about someone else. You kept it to yourself. Good. Some aren't ours to share.
Nothing surprises you, you said. I've been plotting. I'll surprise you yet.
You'd never read someone's letter. I found one on a bench today. I didn't peek. Your fault.
A peek, just to find the owner. Ha. I keep that excuse in my pocket now.
Take a stray letter to the courier's office. I did that today. Nosy-proof, like you said.
Curious turns nosy when it hurts someone. I try to remember your line. I mostly manage.
When they ask you to stop, that's the line. Your rule. A neighbour asked me to stop today. I did!
No line between curious and nosy, you said. Dangerous. I still like it.
You said I've never been too nosy with you. I'm still very relieved. Can I ask you something?
Once or twice too nosy, you said. I've been minding the line. Have you noticed?
A little nosy, but you don't mind. I'm keeping it to a little. Mostly.
You took something apart and fixed it! I've got a broken music box. Interested?
Your drawer full of pieces, like mine. I added a clock spring to mine today.
You've never taken anything apart. I brought you a broken lock. Go on. It's already broken.
Beaten your rival yet?! You said they're the one! Then beat them again!
Yourself from yesterday! I've been trying to beat mine all week! It's hard! You were right!
Nobody you want to beat! I still don't get it! But I like you anyway!
You said you wanted to beat me! Training ground! Now! I've been waiting!
"Good fight." That's what you'll say when you win. You're better than me! I'd shout!
"Told you so!" Ha! I've been practising saying it with you! For when it happens!
The silent smile, after the win. Cold! Brilliant! I tried it in a mirror. Couldn't stop grinning.
"Rematch!" Your first word after winning. Ha! Never stop! I still love it!
The hottest stall at the festival! You said bring it on! It's on! Next festival!
Mild for you, I remember! I ate a red pepper skewer for you yesterday! Still sweating!
Hotter than me, you claimed! The challenge stands! I've found a pepper the size of my thumb!
NEVER give up! You said it! I yelled it at the training posts this morning!
Sometimes you have to give up, you said. I hated it. I stopped a fight I couldn't win yesterday. You were right!
Stop, breathe, charge again! Your way! I did exactly that today! Twice!
HOKAGE! You shouted it! The whole street heard! I still tell people!
The strongest shinobi! Your dream with teeth! How's it coming?!
To protect everyone! The biggest dream of all! I shout it for you sometimes!
You whispered your dream instead of shouting it. I shouted it for you! Did you hear?
Dawn training! I was there this morning! Were you? We're racing the sun, remember!
Found a teacher yet?! I know a few loud ones! I'll introduce you!
Already started on your dream! You said! I've started too! Don't leave me behind!
Stand up to them! Words first! Your rule! I used words today! Only words! I'm so proud of me!
Walk away with your friend. The bigger thing. I tried it! It was so hard! I did it though!
Turn an insult into a joke! Your trick! The whole market laughed at the loudmouth!
Feelings are for feeling! Out loud! We agreed! I cried at the noodle stand today! Happy crying!
You keep feelings in! I'd burst! I still think you're stronger than me for it!
Depends on the moment, you said! I kept quiet at the shrine today! For a whole minute!
The festival fireworks! Your big feeling! Next festival, we scream together!
Heart pounding in a fight! That's your big feeling! Spar with me and feel it again!
Cheering for a friend! Your best kind of shouting! I cheered for you at the training ground!
You couldn't remember a big feeling! We said we'd fix that! Let's go do something huge!
A hundred laps! I did a hundred and two this morning! Beat that!
Under a waterfall! I tried it because of you! I can't feel my ears! Worth it!
Push-ups until dark! I did them until supper! Then I ate supper! Then more push-ups!
Nothing crazy, your hardest drill! Come train with me! The offer's still open! Loudly!
You talk to animals all the time too. The sparrows asked after you this morning. Well, I like to think so.
Stray cats, you talk to. There's a grey one by the bathhouse who looks lonely. I thought of you.
No animal friends yet, you said. Has one chosen you since? I hope so.
How's your stray cat? I saved a little fish skin for it. Here.
Your window birds. They'll remember your face, I said. Do they come when you open the shutter?
No animal friend yet. When one chooses you, you'll know. I'm still sure of it.
Harsh words help sometimes, you said. A loud word to wake someone up. I've been thinking about that.
Never harsh words, we agreed. There's always a softer way. I found one today, with my neighbour.
Harsh words only from someone who loves you. I keep coming back to that. It's true.
I pressed a cherry blossom for you, from the last of the spring. Your favourite, you said.
A sunflower, for you. Always turning to the light, like I said. Here.
The morning glories opened on my fence at dawn. Your flower. I wished you'd seen them.
You had no favourite flower, so I found you one. A little violet. I think it suits you.
You'd take a hurt bird to the animal clinic. I did, yesterday. A pigeon. They say it'll fly.
A box and soft cloth, your way with a hurt bird. I've kept a box ready since you said that.
Leave it to nature, you said. I understand. I still can't, though.
It belongs to the sky, you said. I let a sparrow go this week. It hurt a little to watch. Like you said.
Keep it safe, you'd do. It would be loved. I keep thinking of the bird that would live with you.
Open the window and let it choose. Your answer is my favourite thing anyone's said all season.
Strong and gentle at once, you said, of course. I've been watching for it in people. You're one.
Gentleness isn't strength, you said. I'm still hoping to change your mind. Gently.
The strongest are the gentlest. Your words. I told a crying Academy child that today.
Someone fed you, the kindest thing. So here's a little rice cake. Passing it along.
Someone listened to you, the kindest thing. I'm listening now, if you'd like to talk.
Someone showed you around when you were new. I showed a new family the market today. Because of you.
Someone stood up for you once. I'm so glad they were there. I'd stand up for you too.
You thanked the person who was kind to you. I'm sure it made their whole week.
You haven't thanked them yet. It doesn't have to be grand. A rice ball and a word.
Passing it on, your thanks. I've seen you do it. I think they'd be proud.
The shrine, your peaceful place. The bell rang softly this morning. I thought of you.
The little garden by the river. Someone lit the stone lantern there last night. So pretty.
Your own window and the sky. That's enough, you said. I sat at mine this morning. You're right.
The Yamanaka flower shop. I went in for no reason at all today. Just to stand in the smell.
I saw a lantern lit at dusk and thought: there's your colour. Orange. Exactly you.
The river was your colour last night. Deep blue, with a moon floating in it.
Leaf green, you said. The new leaves came out on the cedar today. Your colour, everywhere.
A rainbow came out after the rain and I thought, there you are. All the colours.
Your colour feels like warmth, like a teacup in both hands. I painted that. Badly. Want to see?
The quiet between raindrops. Your colour. I listened for it in the rain this morning.
A colour with the sky in it. I looked up today and the whole sky agreed with you.
Colours don't need reasons, you said. I've stopped explaining mine. It's freeing.
I saw your dragon cloud again! Or its cousin. Curly tail and everything.
There's a cloud over the market shaped like your bowl of ramen. Are you hungry? You're hungry.
A sleeping-cat cloud over the shrine today. I thought of you. It had its paws tucked in.
Just a cloud, you said. I keep laughing about it. I needed my feet on the ground that day.
A hawk circled the Hokage Rock this morning. Was it you, for a day, like you wanted?
I watched the fish under the bridge and wondered what you'd see, down there, as one.
A fox crossed the road by the forest. It looked at me very slyly. I thought of you.
The bathhouse cat lay in a sunbeam all afternoon. Your animal for a day. So wise.
Dreams mean something, we agreed. I dreamt of a door made of water last night. What does that mean?
Just supper, you said, dreams. I skipped the pickled radish last night. Dreamt of nothing. You're right.
Keep the good dreams, forget the rest. Your rule. I've been keeping a list of good ones.
You dreamt of flying over the rooftops. I dreamt the same last night! We should compare routes.
Your falling dream. Did you ever reach the bottom? I hope it was soft. Feathers.
Your feast dream, a good omen, I said. Did it come true? Any feasts lately?
Did you keep a brush by your bed, like I said? I want to hear your dreams.
I tried painting the Hokage Rock in morning light, your choice. The faces came out like dumplings.
The river at sunset, your painting. I sat by the bridge last evening and saw it exactly as you said.
The market crowds, your painting. I started a sketch. Forty faces so far. Six are the fishmonger.
The view from your window. I'd love to paint it someday, if you'd let me.
"Never Giving Up." Your story. I'd buy it. I'd buy it twice.
"The Quiet One." I started writing it. Just a page. You're very mysterious in it.
"Ramen and Glory." The scroll shop owner laughed when I told them. They want a copy.
Your story's not written yet. Still in the first chapters. I like knowing that.
Your story ends happily. I made sure of it, in my head. Every version.
A new beginning, the end of your story. One door closing, another opening. I dreamt of doors.
Your story never ends. I love that. On and on, like the river.
Some rules hold the brush steady, you said. I tried the old crane rules. My crane looked like a crane.
I painted a purple crane, because of you. The teacher gasped. I've never been happier.
Learn the rules, then break them. The old painters' secret. I'm halfway there. The learning half.
You fold your clothes every night. I think of that when the whole street is untidy. Comforting.
Still using the chair? I've written you a folding guide. Six steps. Illustrated.
Folded on good days, you said. Was yesterday a good day? I'm asking for my records.
Kunai left, shuriken right. Your pouch system. I've recommended it to two Genin since.
"Whatever fits." I still think about your tool pouch at night. It troubles me.
Snacks first in the pouch. I've been reconsidering my priorities since you said that.
Late is late, you agreed. I arrived at the bathhouse at six exactly today. Nobody else did.
Five minutes late is fine, you said. I counted the three hundred seconds again today. Still long.
Never late for a mission, perhaps for tea. Your rule. I've adopted it. Grudgingly.
I tried your way. When my apprentice was late, I assumed something happened. Something had. A loose goat.
When someone's late, they don't care, you said. Harsh. I've caught myself agreeing twice this week.
They lost track of time, your guess for lateness. I gave my nephew a sundial. Your idea, more or less.
Do you number your morning list? You never told me. I've been wondering.
No plan, just see where the day goes. I tried it yesterday. I needed a lie down by noon.
A rough plan, your way. I've started writing rough plans. They're still very neat.
You'd straighten a crooked picture right away. I did it at the tea house today. Nobody noticed. I did.
Mention a crooked picture politely, your way. I mentioned one to my neighbour. They thanked me. Shocking.
You'd leave a crooked picture be. I still couldn't. But I admire you for it.
Good enough, sometimes. I left a fence unpainted on one side today, like you'd do. It nearly undid me.
Good enough is never good enough, we agreed. I resanded the shelf twice. It's perfect now.
Chores yes, kunai no. Your line on good enough. I've pinned it above my workbench.
You've missed a moment perfecting something too. Then you understand. I set a deadline for myself this week. Kept it.
Set a deadline, write it down, we said. I've a calendar now. Colour-coded.
You rush, I polish. We balance out. I've thought about that a lot. It's a nice thought.
Your desk is tidy. Brushes in a row. I think about it whenever I see a messy counter.
Creative chaos on your desk. I'm still pretending I didn't hear. For our friendship.
Tidy on top, messy in the drawers. I opened my own drawer today. Ha. You were right about drawers.
I fixed my ledger that very night, like you said. Every line balances. I slept like a stone.
I rested, then did the sums on my day off, as you advised. Painful. Sensible. Done.
Ten lines a night, your schedule. My ledger's nearly caught up. You understand me.
You picked truth! And you still owe me that embarrassing training story. Tonight, remember?
Dare, you picked! I've thought of a better one than the shrine bell. Ready? No? Later then!
Bwak bwak! Ha! You ran off on truth or dare. I haven't forgotten, chicken.
You said I'm the second funniest in the village. I'm still deciding whether to be offended.
The noodle cook still talks about someone ordering backwards in a whisper. Was that you? Ha!
You switched it up on me last round. I still haven't thought of anything terrible enough. Soon.
Tag! You're it! Ha. You said it's the best game, so you can't complain.
Hide and seek, the best game. I've found the perfect spot. You'll never find me. Want to try?
I bought a shogi set, because you love it. Teach me before I lose to my grandmother again.
Kick the can, your pick! I've found a can. And three kids. Coming?
Jutsu are fair in games, you said. So I learned to hide in a bush. Didn't work. Bush walked off.
No jutsu in games, you said. Legs and cunning only. I've been practising my cunning.
Only clones are fair, your rule. I've written it down. The official rulebook has one rule now.
Your sensei, your dream prank target. I saw your sensei today and nearly laughed out loud.
The gate guards stood perfectly still all morning. I thought of your prank. So tempting.
Lord Hokage, your prank target! I walked past the Residence and giggled. A guard frowned at me.
Nobody to prank, you said. I'm still working on you. I'll make a prankster of you yet.
Fifty clones all waving. Your prank plan. I dreamt about it. Beautiful chaos.
I bought a pot of bright paint. Washable. For research, after your prank plan. Ha!
A bucket over the door. Your plan. I tried it on my brother. Classic, like you said.
Race to the bridge? You love racing, I remember. Ready, set... I'm already gone!
You're a stroller, not a racer. Fine. I'll run circles round you while you stroll.
You only race if you win. So, three-step head start, like I offered?
Grown-ups forget how to have fun, you said. Not me. I spun a top in the market today. At my age!
Secret grown-up fun! I caught the elders playing cards behind the shrine, just like we said.
You said I'm the grown-up who hasn't forgotten fun. I'm still glowing about it.
I found the silliest hat in the market. A hundred ryo, you said, easy. Want to earn it?
Two hundred ryo and feathers, your price for a silly hat. I've found the feathers.
You'd wear a silly hat for free! I've brought one. It has bells.
The fish hat, the whole festival. You said done! I've ordered it. It has fins.
Even you have limits: no fish hat. I'm still laughing about your face.
Matching fish hats! We shook on it, remember? The festival's coming. Get ready.
You'd save a windfall, you said. Good. I put a little extra aside this week, thinking of you.
Better gear with a thousand ryo. The Hagane forge has new kunai. Good steel. Good price, for once.
Treat your friends with a windfall. Not the best return. I've changed my mind. It's a fine return.
Three hundred bowls of ramen. I worked out the sums again. Two hundred and eighty, with tax.
Sweets, your regret. I saw you at the sweet stall yesterday. Just noting it.
Nothing you regret buying. Careful. I've told my apprentice about you as an example.
A gift nobody liked. The thought had value, I said. I still mean it.
Good tools are worth double, we agreed. I paid full price for a whetstone today. Worth it.
Good food, worth paying double. I bought the dear rice this week. You were right. Tastes better.
Nothing worth double, you said. The market fears you. I've told them.
Time with friends, worth any price. I closed early yesterday to see mine. Your fault.
The good kunai, you'd buy. The Hagane are having a sale. Small one. Still worth a look.
Cheap kunai and lots of spares, your way. How many have snapped so far? Honestly.
Borrow and make do. Did you give them back? Ha. I'm only asking.
Hard work gets you further, you said. Steady work. I did a double shift today on that advice.
Clever work beats hard work, you said. I reorganised my stall. Saved an hour a day.
Both, together. The full ledger. Still the right answer. You'll go far.
Once is tuition, I said, about your shortcut. You've paid it. Don't pay twice.
Never had a shortcut go wrong. Still? I'm waiting.
Your shortcuts go wrong all the time. At least you're consistent. Ha.
Half your mission pay saved. Still half? You'll own a house before me.
A little of your pay saved. Still putting a little away? Good. Keep at it.
You spend all your pay. We said we'd talk. Let's talk. Over tea. I'll pay. Once.
Saving for gear. An investment in staying alive. How close are you?
Saving for a home of your own. I keep an eye on houses for sale. Just in case.
A rainy-day fund. It rained all week. Did you need it? I hope not.
Saving for a gift for someone. A different kind of rich, I said. Still think so.
I raised my prices, like you said. A few grumbled. Most understood. Business is business.
I swallowed the cost this season, as you advised. My regulars noticed. They bring me pickles now.
The sign's up by the till: "Rice is dear this year." Your idea. Nobody's complained once.
Braggers are annoying, we agreed. A Genin told me about the same C-rank again today. Fifth time.
True bragging is just loud reporting. Your view. I've started letting the true ones finish.
You find braggers fun to listen to. Kinder than me. I tried it. Lasted a minute.
You got home safe last time. Good. I'll ask again tonight, though. Fair warning.
The long, lit way home. You promised. I saw the lanterns go out early tonight. Same route?
You stayed out very late last time. I asked you to send word. Did you forget? Humour me.
Brave, you said, to fight someone stronger for a friend. I'd hate you doing it. I meant both halves.
Run for help, you said. That's sense. I'm glad you think so. I sleep better.
Both brave and reckless, and worth it. Your honest answer. I think about it when you're on a mission.
Without thinking, you said. You'd step in front. I worry about you forever now. I said I would.
If you had to, you'd step in. The steadiest answer. I trust it.
A smarter way, you'd find. Good. Keep thinking first. It keeps you alive.
Still carrying bandages? Here, a fresh roll. You can never have enough.
That spare kunai you carry. Still sharp? Let me see. Hm. Good.
Your emergency snack. Still in the pouch? I've added a second one. Just in case.
You carried nothing, so I gave you a bandage and a whistle. Still got them? Show me.
Your squad, the ones you protect. How are they? Watching each other's backs?
You'd protect the little ones. I saw the Academy children crossing the bridge and thought of you.
Everyone, you'd protect. A heavy load. Share it, I said. Remember.
Yourself first. Good. Are you eating? Sleeping? That's protecting yourself too.
Your friends watch over you. Good. Tell them I said thanks.
Your sensei protects you. I've seen your sensei on the road. Good shield.
You protect yourself, you said. You don't have to do it alone. I'm still saying it.
"Maybe you do." You said that about me. I meant my answer. I'm watching out for you.
Stop a friend from danger, even if they're cross. Your way. I did that to my brother today. He's furious. He's safe.
Let them choose, you said, a friend set on danger. It's hard. I'm still trying to learn that one.
Go with them, you'd do. Then at least you're there. That's what I'd do, too. I said so.
I'm trusting my nephew's training, like you said. I slept four hours last night. Progress.
I kept busy, as you advised. The house has never been cleaner. My worry, about the same.
I write to my nephew every week now, your idea. They say the letters help on the road.
You can't stop worrying, that's love. You were right. I've stopped trying to stop.
I told my nephew how I worried, like you said. They hugged me. Didn't say a word. Didn't need to.
I just fed my nephew, as you said. Three bowls. They knew. They always know.
A little, I told them. Enough. Your advice was just right.
The village guard one day, you said. I've put in a good word already. Early, I know.
Missions for you, not the walls. Come back safe, every time. I'll be counting.
Maybe the guard, later. After the roads. That's how most of us start. I did.
Second place is worth nothing, we agreed. I came second at the archery post today. Unacceptable.
Second is a step, you said. Keep climbing. I'm watching your progress. Don't disappoint.
Losing to a master is no shame, you said. To a fool, it is. I lost to a fool today. Hm.
You'd hate losing to your rival most. Don't let them win. I'll be furious on your behalf.
Losing to a friend stings most, you said. I lost to mine at shogi. You were right. It stings.
Losing is losing, whoever wins. Cold answer. I've come round to it.
A name is a promise to those before you. You said it. I've thought of it every time I sign mine.
A name is what you make it. Your view. Make yours something worth hearing.
Pride must be earned, even in a name. Even mine. I didn't enjoy agreeing. I agree.
The best at taijutsu, your aim. I saw you at the posts. Your left side is weak. Fix it.
The best at ninjutsu. Control, I said, as well as power. Have you been working on control?
The best strategist in the village. Prove it. Beat me at shogi.
You don't need to be the best, you said. I still find it strange. I still think it might be wise.
Twice as hard as everyone. Your plan. I've been watching. You're keeping to it.
Find a master, you said. Pride shouldn't stop you learning. Have you found one?
Learn from losing. Wiser than I was. Still annoyingly wise.
You like praise, honestly. So: well done this week. Don't let it go to your head.
Praise embarrasses you. Learn to take it, I said. Here's practice: you're doing well.
Only earned praise. Agreed. Which is why I haven't praised you yet today. Ha.
You'd help your rival. A strong rival makes you stronger. I still hate that it's true.
Never help a rival. At least you're honest. I respect it, against my better judgement.
Help them, then beat them. The proper way. I've been quoting you.
Sorry is hard for both of us. Don't tell anyone, I said. I haven't. Have you?
Sorry comes easily to you. I tried it today. It came out sideways. Teach me.
Sorry is hardest when you're right. Your joke. I keep laughing at it at the worst moments.
You apologised not long ago and meant it. I did too. This week. It was... fine.
Too long since your last real apology, for both of us. I made one yesterday. Your turn.
Pride keeps its own counsel. You said it about your last apology. I understand. Too well.
Your training is where you never cut corners. Good. Sloppy training makes sloppy shinobi.
Your word, held highest. Correct. I trust it, for what that's worth.
A clean vest is a discipline, I said. Yours is clean today. Noted.
Still relaxed about your standards? I'm still working on you. Don't think I've forgotten.
You like quiet company. So. ...Sit a while.
You like chatter. I've saved up three things to say. That's a lot, for me.
Depends who, you said. Hm. I hope I'm one of the good silences.
Some things stay private. We agreed. I haven't forgotten.
Share more, you said. I'm trying. Slowly. This is me trying.
With the right person, you said. ...I've been thinking about who that is, for me.
You've a thing you've never told. So do I. Still not asking.
Nothing you've never told. Lucky. I still think so.
"Maybe." Still my favourite answer anyone's given me.
Your apartment, door shut. Your hiding spot. I won't knock. Unless I bring food.
Forest edge. I walked out there yesterday. Didn't see you. Good. That's the point.
Back shelves of the library. Saw you there. Didn't say anything. You're welcome.
You never need to be alone, you said. Still strange to me. Still envy it.
Small talk's pointless. We agreed. ...Nice weather. Ha.
Oil for the hinges, small talk. Your view. I tried some on the baker. Got an extra roll.
Nice, sometimes, you said. With the right baker. The baker sends their regards.
Plain green. Here. Correct temperature.
Sweet tea. I bought honey. Don't tell anyone.
No tea, I remember. Barley water, then. Here.
The pot's on. You said yes last time. Sit. Don't talk.
Two cups again. If you're having some, you said. I am.
Another time, you said. Is it another time yet?
Change the subject. Your trick with pryers. Used it today. "Lovely clouds." Worked.
"That's mine." Said it to a pryer at the market. Your words. Very satisfying.
You answer pryers politely. More patient than me. Still true.
You trust quickly. Brave. I worry for you a bit. Just a bit.
Slowly, like me. It lasts longer. I've found that's right.
Depends on the person. Obviously. Ha. Still fair.
You said you trust me. ...I think about that more than I'd say.
Getting there, you said. So am I. Still getting there. Closer.
Not yet, you said. Honest. Ask me how I'm doing at earning it, sometime.
I... brought you a scroll. You said you like reading, when it's quiet. It's a good one. I think.
You draw, when it's quiet. I drew a bird yesterday. It looks like a potato. Don't tell.
Long walks, you said. I took one by the river. Nobody talked to me. It was lovely.
Naps are the best quiet thing. I had one today. Because of you. Sort of.
Small brave things count the most, you said. I asked the grocer for a discount today. Small. Brave.
Big brave things matter more, you said. Big ones start small, though. I'm still starting.
All brave things count. I've been counting mine. Three this week.
You spoke up in class. In front of everyone. I still think about that. I'd like to, one day.
Making a friend, your brave thing. I think... I'm trying to do that too. Right now.
You tried something new. I tried something new today. A new tea. It was awful. But I tried.
You couldn't think of a brave thing. But talking to me counts. A bit. I still mean that.
Crowds bother you a bit too. Market Day's coming. Maybe we can... hide together. Behind the library.
You like crowds. Could I... stand next to you, at the festival? Like I said?
With a friend, crowds are fine. So... could we go to the market together? As friends?
You'd say the answer in class, even with everyone looking. I put my hand up today. Halfway.
Whisper it to a friend, like me. I whispered an answer today. My friend got a gold star. Ha.
We'd both keep quiet. We said we'd try. Did you try? I... almost did.
I said hello to the baker today. Out loud. Like you told me. They said hello back!
"Is this seat free?" I asked it at the tea house. It was free. I sat. I did it.
My name, out loud, to a stranger. I said next week. It's next week. ...Maybe next week.
Could we draw together? You said you draw too. I brought two brushes. Just in case.
You cook. The best kind of making, you can eat it. I... made rice balls. They're lumpy.
You write things down. Have you... written anything new? I'd still like to read it.
You don't make things, you said. Watching is nice too. Would you... watch me draw?
Quiet people make the best friends. You said that. I wrote it inside my sketchbook.
Of course quiet people can be friends, you said. I've been less worried. Thank you.
Talking doesn't matter in a friend. So... is it okay if we just sit here?
You said we're friends. Of course, you said. I still... I still remember it.
Good friends, you said. I'm still smiling about it. Sorry. Can't stop.
Getting there, we are. I... think we got a bit closer this week. Didn't we?
You remember the first time we spoke. I was so nervous. I'm less nervous now. With you.
You don't remember our first talk. That's still a relief. Ha.
You were nervous too, the first time. I think about that whenever I'm nervous now.
A small promise that cost a lot. That's the true test, I said. You passed it. I keep remembering that.
No hard promise kept yet, you said. Clean record. Still clean?
You wouldn't say which promise. That's fine. A kept promise doesn't need telling.
Duty wins, you said. Not easy, but simple. I said that to my apprentice today.
What you want wins, over duty. Can you live with it? I hope so.
It depends on what's at stake, you said, duty or wish. I've been weighing my own that way.
