Duty cost you something once. I'm still proud of you for it. Both things are true.
Duty hasn't cost you yet. When it does, come talk to me. You'll know what you're made of.
You'd pay duty's cost again. That's steel. I've told people so.
Same routine every day, you said. I saw the sun come up at the usual time and thought of yours.
You like variety in your days. Keep one thing steady, I said. Found your one thing yet?
Mostly the same routine. Most of us are mostly. I still say so.
You'd cover a friend's shift, tired or not. I've a strong tea here. For next time.
A tired guard is half a guard. You were right. I said no to an extra shift this week.
Find someone else to cover it. That's what you'd do. I did, when my partner asked. Worked well.
You lean on your squad. Good. How is your squad holding up?
Your teacher's the one you rely on. Tell them that someday. It matters.
You rely on yourself most. Don't make it only yourself, I said. Lean on me too, if need be.
One good friend, the one you lean on. Hold on to them.
Your squad leans on you. Carry it well. You are.
No one relies on you yet, you said. I do, now. So there's one.
More people rely on you than you know. You said it yourself. I'm one of them.
You'd promise to protect the Leaf. Said plainly. I remember it whenever I see you on the road.
Never leave the Leaf, your promise. I believed you then. I still do.
Make the Leaf proud, your promise. You're doing it already, in small ways.
Training every day, rain or shine. That's how you keep your promise. I've seen the proof.
Helping where you can. A promise kept quietly. I noticed, you know.
Showing up. Half of duty is just being there, you said. I've repeated it a dozen times since.
Honest with a friend even when it hurts. That's your rule. I'll expect nothing less from you.
You'd spare a friend a painful truth. Kind. I'm still not sure I could.
The truth wrapped in care. Your way. I tried it on my brother. It went well.
You train when no one's watching, you said. I've been watching. You weren't lying. Good.
You train when you feel like it. Have you felt like it this week? Think on what I said.
Your own drills, unwatched. Acceptable, if you do them. Are you doing them?
You skipped training that week. Don't make it two, I said. Did you?
Never skipped training, you said. Keep it that way. I'll know.
You couldn't remember your last skipped session. Too long ago, or too often? I'm still waiting.
Discipline over talent. Correct. Talent is a loan. Pay it back daily.
You chose talent over discipline. Wrong, mostly. Prove me wrong by working.
Talent wins early, discipline late. Your answer. I've repeated it to three Genin.
Patience, your weakness. Ten minutes still, every day. Have you sat?
Chakra control, your weak point. Leaf-balancing every night. No shortcuts. I said it. I meant it.
Your guard drops. You admitted it. I watched you spar. It still drops. Fix it.
You didn't know your weakness. Found it yet? Before an enemy does?
Drilling your weakness daily, you said. A month's nearly up. Report.
You asked for help with your weakness. Pride beaten. Good. The second victory is the harder one.
Nothing done about your weakness, you said. I said tomorrow, at dawn. It is past tomorrow.
Obey, then ask. Your answer on a wrong order. Correct. Remember it when it's hard.
Speak up once, clearly. Then obey. That's how you'd handle a wrong order. Good.
Obey, then report. Use the chain, I said. Have you had to yet?
Lateness is a small fault, you said. Small faults grow. I'm watching yours.
Lateness is disrespect. You agreed. You were on time today. Noted.
Depends on the cause, you said. A sick child, fine. Breakfast, no. I hold to that.
You rise before dawn. I saw a lamp in your window early. Good.
Dawn, you rise. An hour earlier, I said. Have you tried?
You rise late. We said we'd fix it. We haven't. Tomorrow.
You rise to train. The right answer. Still the right answer.
Habit, why you rise. Discipline that stopped complaining. I'm pleased with that phrase. It was mine.
You like sleep. Honest. Sleep is training, up to a point. Have you passed the point?
Comfort is where strength naps. You agreed. I slept on the floor last night. Out of principle.
Rest matters, you said. I conceded it. I took a full day's rest this week. Do not tell anyone.
A little comfort, earned. Your rule. You've earned a little this week. Take it.
People become shinobi to protect others, you said. I found a scroll from the founding that agrees with you.
Glory, you said, is why people choose the life. I counted the statues in the village. You may have a point.
Family expectation, your reason. I've been noticing how many shinobi share a parent's trade.
"Because they can." I keep returning to that answer of yours. It's simpler than mine, and maybe truer.
You chose this path to protect people. I've watched you since. It holds.
You wanted to matter to someone. I wrote that in my notebook. You do, you know.
Not sure yet why you chose the path. I respect that more than any certainty.
Always better to know, you said. A painful truth at least stands still. I've quoted us both since.
Not always better to know. I've been testing your answer on the world. It keeps passing.
Truth needs someone ready to hold it. That came from our talk. I think of it often.
A history, your one scroll. The library has a new one on the founding clans. I set it aside for you.
One scroll of jutsu, forever. I imagined you as that hermit. A cheerful one.
A book of stories, your one scroll. Have you found the one you'd read a hundred times?
A blank scroll, to fill yourself. Have you started writing in it? I'd read it.
The past is the teacher, we said. I've been reading old village records because of that.
The future matters most to you. Where we'll live. I've been trying to look forward more.
"Only today." I wrote it on a slip of paper and pinned it over my desk.
You'd change that one choice, even at the cost of its lesson. I've wondered which choice it was. I won't ask.
Your mistakes made you, you said, and you'd keep them. I admire that peace.
You needed to think about whether you'd change it. Have you? There's no hurry.
I told the librarian about a wrong date myself, the way you said you would. They thanked me warmly.
You'd correct a library scroll yourself. Bold. I found one of your sort of corrections in the margins today. Not yours, I hope?
A note left inside the scroll for the next reader. I did it. Your idea was too good not to.
Quiet people are underestimated, you agreed. Still water. I've been listening to the quiet ones more since.
Quiet as a choice, not a lack. You said that. It changed how I see a few people I know.
"We all see each other through a keyhole." I keep using your thought in arguments. I win them.
You want to understand people, by the end. I found a scroll on it. It's no help at all. Ha.
Chakra, the thing you'd most like to understand. The scroll keepers have a new treatise. I'll show you.
To understand yourself, that's your hope. The oldest question. How's it going?
Understanding everything, you said. Have you started? Tonight, I told you.
Ask, listen, ask again. Your method. I've been asking more questions because of it.
You'll read everything to learn it. The good shelves are at the back of the library, by the window. I'm there most mornings.
Live and watch, your slow way of learning. I watched the river for an hour today. Learned a lot, actually.
I made a pot of miso soup and kept a bowl back. You said soup cheers you up. Here, still hot.
Sweet buns, red bean and custard, both. You said they cheer you up. You looked like you needed one.
Rice and pickles, wrapped up for you. Plain and honest, like you said. Eat it before training.
I made you something. You said anything someone makes for you helps. So here's my something.
Supper's on, the one I promised. Come hungry, I said, and I meant it. There's enough for six.
Ready for your cooking lesson? You wanted to learn the recipe. Apron's on the hook.
Together, you said, or not at all. So I've set two bowls. Sit.
A proper meal again today? Good. You said so last time too. I'm keeping track.
Just a snack again? I remember last time. Here, a proper lunch. No arguments.
You forgot to eat last time I asked. So I've brought rice balls. Three of them. Eat.
You manage on your own when you're poorly. I've been worrying about that ever since.
Your friends look after you when you're unwell. Tell them I've got extra blankets if they need them.
The hospital looks after you if it's bad. And for colds? Me. I've decided.
